lines.text: Most data platforms are written by hand, one layer at a time, and each layer drifts from the last.
Here, you declare what you have, and generators write the rest.
Ingest is where data arrives. A short file declares what a source serves.
Ingest lands every load in the lake, as it came, so nothing is ever lost.
Each resource gets its own pipeline, so one failure never halts the rest.
Conform gives raw rows a shape. A data contract types each field and marks its key.
Why? A contract is a promise. A value that breaks it is flagged, never trusted.
Every contract becomes a staged model, generated, never written by hand.
Integrate is the memory of the business. An Anchor model declares what the business knows.
Why? Sources come and go, but the business stays. Every change is kept, with when it was true, and when we learned it.
As more sources are declared, the same model grows, one anchor at a time.
Serve is where questions get answered. From the same model, it generates a Unified Star Schema.
Why? So anyone can join anything to anything, through one bridge, without knowing how it was built.
Today serve generates a star. Because it is generated, other shapes can follow.
One schedule ties it together. Every source is ingested on its own, then the platform builds once.
